# Model-upgrade experiment — Sonnet 4.5 → Opus 4.8

**Question:** the production corpus was generated by Claude Sonnet 4.5.
Would a stronger model (Opus 4.8) produce a better alignment + apparatus,
and is the improvement *directional* (measurable on proxies, since we have
no gold standard)?

**Method:** ran Mark 13 (the variant-rich, hand-audited chapter) **twice**
on `claude-opus-4-8` with `output_config.effort = medium`, plus Mark 1:1
twice, then measured three things against the existing Sonnet data and the
four hand-verified errors from the 2026-04-30 audit. Cost: ~$5, ~15 min.

> **Why "directional" and not "better"?** There is no ground-truth
> alignment to score against — that is the whole reason scholar review
> matters. So we measure *proxies*: self-consistency (precision),
> avoidance of known errors (the only real ground truth we have, N=4),
> and cross-model divergence. Improvement on proxies is suggestive, not
> conclusive. A better model makes a better draft, not a critical edition.

---

## Result 1 — Known-error avoidance (the ground-truth signal)

The audit gave us four apparatus claims a human verified were **wrong** in
the original Sonnet output (see `data/alignments/CHANGELOG.md`). We check
whether each model run *repeats* or *avoids* each error.

| Run | Mark 13:14 ܐܬܐ | Mark 1:1 ܕ- | Mark 1:1 ܒܪܗ suffix | Mark 1:1 article | Total avoided |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sonnet production (original) | ✗ repeat | ✗ repeat | ✗ repeat | ✗ repeat | 0/4 *(these are the audit errors)* |
| Sonnet run #2 (fresh, same model) | ✗ repeat | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | **3/4** |
| **Opus 4.8 run 1** | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | **4/4** |
| **Opus 4.8 run 2** | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | ✓ avoid | **4/4** |

Two findings:

1. **Three of the four audit errors were single-run flukes.** A fresh
   Sonnet run (#2) already avoids them — they were noise in the original
   sample, not systematic Sonnet failures. (This is consistent with the
   ~35% inter-run instability measured earlier.)
2. **The Mark 13:14 ܐܬܐ error is systematic for Sonnet** — both the
   original and the fresh run get it wrong (calling the noun ܐܬܐ, "sign,"
   a "demonstrative pronoun"). **Opus 4.8 gets it right in both
   independent runs.** This is the cleanest accuracy signal in the
   experiment: a verified error that Sonnet reliably makes and Opus 4.8
   reliably avoids.

Caveat: N=4 is a tiny ground-truth set. "4/4 avoided" is encouraging, not
statistically robust.

---

## Result 2 — Self-consistency (precision)

Each model run twice, same prompt, same inputs. How much does the model
agree with *itself* across runs? Higher = tighter distribution = less
coin-flipping on ambiguous partitions.

| Metric | Sonnet 4.5 × Sonnet 4.5 | Opus 4.8 × Opus 4.8 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group-membership overlap | 65% | **76%** | **+11 pp** |
| Verdict agreement (shared groups) | 86% | **90%** | +4 pp |
| Semantic-type agreement (shared groups) | 70% | **76%** | +6 pp |

Opus 4.8 is directionally more self-consistent on **all three** precision
metrics. But note the floor persists: a quarter of alignment groups still
disagree between two Opus runs. The task ambiguity is lower with the
stronger model, not gone.

(Sonnet baseline = full-Mark consensus, `docs/sonnet-consensus-mark.md`;
Opus baseline = Mark 13 only, 35 verses with both runs valid.)

---

## Result 3 — Cross-model divergence

How different are the two models' outputs for the same verse?
(Opus 4.8 run 1 vs Sonnet production, Mark 13.)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Group-membership overlap | 42% |
| Verdict agreement (shared groups) | 71% |
| Type agreement (shared groups) | 31% |
| Apparatus-note prose similarity | 0.15 |

The two models produce **substantially different corpora** — only 42%
group overlap. This is *more* divergence than Opus-vs-Opus (76%) or
Sonnet-vs-Sonnet (65%), confirming the models genuinely differ rather than
sampling the same distribution. The low prose similarity (0.15) means the
apparatus annotations are almost entirely rewritten between models.

---

## Result 4 — Confidence still uncalibrated

| Run | Avg self-reported confidence |
|---|---|
| Sonnet 4.5 | 0.878 |
| Opus 4.8 | 0.872 |

Despite all the disagreement above, both models self-report ~0.87
confidence. **Self-reported confidence remains useless as a quality
signal**, regardless of model tier. The earlier methodology disclaimer
stands unchanged.

---

## Result 5 — Schema robustness

Both models occasionally emit structurally-invalid alignment (out-of-bounds
token indices) that the schema validator quarantines:

| Run | Quarantined / 37 |
|---|---|
| Opus 4.8 run 1 | 1 |
| Opus 4.8 run 2 | 3 |
| Opus 4.5 (yesterday) | 1 |
| Sonnet 4.5 (full Mark) | 18 / 678 ≈ 1/37 |

Opus 4.8 is **not** structurally error-free — comparable failure rate.
The validator + quarantine step remains necessary.

---

## Verdict

**Directional improvement is real and measured.** On every proxy we can
measure, Opus 4.8 is better or equal:

- ✅ Avoids 4/4 known errors in both runs (vs Sonnet 3/4 fresh, 0/4 original) — including the one systematic Sonnet error
- ✅ +11 pp more self-consistent on group membership (76% vs 65%)
- ✅ +4–6 pp more consistent on verdict + type
- ➖ Confidence still uncalibrated (no model fixes this)
- ➖ Schema-failure rate comparable (no model fixes this)
- ➖ A quarter of groups still unstable across runs (task ambiguity floor persists, just lower)

**What this justifies:** a full re-run of the corpus on Opus 4.8 as a new
major version (`2.0.0`), with the v1→v2 delta published in the CHANGELOG.
The versioning infrastructure built earlier exists precisely for this.

**What this does NOT change:** the honest framing. Opus 4.8 produces a
*better draft*, demonstrably — but "better than Sonnet on 4 test points
and more self-consistent" is not "correct," and is not a substitute for
human scholar review. The methodology disclaimer stays.

---

## Reproduce

```bash
# Two Opus 4.8 runs of Mark 13 (effort=medium)
for r in run1 run2; do
  PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/generate_alignments.py --full --chapter 13 \
    --model claude-opus-4-8 --effort medium \
    --out-root data/_compare/opus48_mark13_$r/alignments --force
  PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/generate_alignments.py --verse Mark 1 1 \
    --model claude-opus-4-8 --effort medium \
    --out-root data/_compare/opus48_mark13_$r/alignments
done

# Known-error check
PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/check_known_errors.py \
  --root data/_compare/opus48_mark13_run1/alignments --label "Opus 4.8 run 1"

# Self-consistency
PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/consensus_alignment.py \
  --root data/_compare/opus48_mark13_run1/alignments \
  --root data/_compare/opus48_mark13_run2/alignments \
  --book mark --out /tmp/opus48_consensus --report-md /tmp/opus48_selfconsistency.md

# Cross-model
PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/compare_sonnet_opus.py \
  --sonnet-root data/alignments \
  --opus-root data/_compare/opus48_mark13_run1/alignments \
  --chapter 13 --out /tmp/opus48_vs_sonnet.md
```

Requires `anthropic>=0.105.0` (Opus 4.8 `output_config.effort`; temperature
is deprecated on that model).
